about: MIDI-capable hardware (1983-) researched maker by maker, compared with the firmware collection (docs/FIRMWARE_CHECKLIST.md). Docs: node tools/firmware/midi_devices_report.mjs. Device fields: midi.din (in/out/thru), midi.usb, firmware.storage (where the OS lives / how it is updated), firmware.officialDownload (maker publishes the update), versions (known OS versions), inCollection (false, or the matching checklist device and its files), match (checklist names to match; "-" = never), sources (per maker). midiUpgrades: third-party MIDI retrofit kits for devices built without MIDI, from the kit makers' own pages ({maker, product, url, firmware: folder in z:/firmwares or why there is none}); those devices have midi.retrofit = true. kitInCollection: set instead of inCollection when the collection has only retrofit-kit firmware for the device (folders marked "factory": false in tools/firmware/download/also.json); such devices stay in the wanted list. removedNoMidi: devices taken out because they have no MIDI (no DIN, no USB-MIDI, no factory MIDI version) and no known third-party MIDI upgrade.
categories: Controllers, master keyboards, wind and drum controllers
Expansion boards, cards and sound ROMs

Roland.note: Synths, samplers, drums, sound modules, effects, sequencers and interfaces covered; digital pianos (HP/LX/FP/RD) and organs (Atelier, VR) only the main models.
Roland.status: partial: HP/LX/FP digital pianos, home organs, V-Drums kits and DJ gear only main models

Boss.note: Roland's guitar/effects brand; only products with MIDI (most compact pedals have none).

Edirol.note: Roland's computer-music brand 1999-2011; SD/UM modules are filed under Roland.

Rodgers.note: Church and theatre organs; most since the mid-1980s have MIDI; only module/representative lines listed.

Yamaha.note: Pro instruments, modules, effects, mixers covered; PSR/PSS/Clavinova/Electone consumer lines only the MIDI-relevant main models.

Korg.note: Korg updates are on korg.com product download pages and in the Korg System Updater (the collection has the latter's packages for recent products).
Korg.status: partial: home pianos, DJ/KAOSS line only main models

Akai.note: Akai Professional; MPC OS updates are on akaipro.com product pages (current and many legacy models).

Casio.note: Pro and MIDI-capable home models; most toy/home keyboards (SA/MT/PT/VL/SK) have no MIDI.
Casio.status: partial: CTK/WK/LK/Privia/Celviano home lines only main models

Kawai.note: Synths/modules complete as far as known; digital pianos only the stage/MIDI-relevant ones.

Ensoniq.note: OS disks for EPS/ASR/TS were sold and are widely archived (Ensoniq user groups, Rubber Chicken); ROM-based units need EPROM dumps.

E-mu.note: E-mu downloads (EOS, Proteus 2000 family flash) were hosted by Creative until ~2015 and survive in archives.

Kurzweil.note: K2000-K2661 OS updates were published as floppy/SysEx files; PC3/Forte/Artis/PC4/K2700/K2088 updates are official downloads.

Alesis.note: Most 1986-2000 units hold the OS in a socketed EPROM (version on the label); QS/S4 OS updates were also sold on ROM cards and SysEx.

Oberheim.note: Gibson-era (1988-) and Viscount-made (OB3, OB-12) products included; modern OB-6/OB-X8/Teo-5 updates are official downloads.

Sequential.note: Includes Dave Smith Instruments (2002-2018) and Sequential LLC (2018-); all DSI/Sequential OS updates are official SysEx downloads.

Moog.note: Moog Music Inc. (2002-) firmware updates are official downloads (SysEx or Moog updater).

Waldorf.note: Q/microQ/Blofeld/Quantum/Iridium OS updates are official MIDI/USB downloads; Microwave I/II/XT used EPROM/flash and SysEx updates.

Access.note: All Virus OS versions were official MIDI/SysEx (A/B/C/Classic/Rack XL) or Virus Control installer (TI) downloads.

Clavia.note: Every Nord OS is an official download (SysEx for Nord Lead 1-3/Modular, Nord Sound Manager/Updater for later models).

Novation.note: Older OS (Supernova, Nova, K/A/X-Station) were official SysEx downloads; current products update through Novation Components.

Elektron.note: All OS updates are official downloads (SysEx or Elektron Transfer).

Lexicon.note: EPROM-based until the late 1990s (version on the chip label); PCM96/MX series updated over USB.

Eventide.note: H3000-era OS in EPROMs (version and options on the label); DSP4000 onward updated by disk/MIDI/USB; Factor pedals, H9, H90 and H9000 are official downloads.

TC Electronic.note: TC published SysEx/MIDI updates for most rack units (G-Major, G-Force, M-One, M3000, Nova) and USB updaters later.

TC-Helicon.note: Vocal processors; firmware updates are official downloads (VoiceSupport app for recent ones).

Line 6.note: All firmware since the POD 2.0 era updates via Line 6 Monkey/Updater/HX Edit (official).

DigiTech.note: Harman-era; DSP/GSP/TSR/Vocalist racks hold the OS in EPROM; GNX/RP USB models had official updates (now on Harman archives).

DOD.note: DigiTech's sister brand; only MIDI models.

Zoom.note: Early racks and multitrackers (9000 series, MRS) are EPROM/flash; current products update by official downloads.

Peavey.note: DPM synths load OS updates from floppy/SysEx; the DPM 3 OS was sold as ROM or disk updates.

ART.note: Applied Research and Technology; OS in EPROM.

Behringer.note: Synths (2017-) update through the official SynthTribe app; older racks/controllers had official SysEx/USB updates, some still downloadable.
Behringer.status: partial: eurorack modules and small USB controllers not listed

ADA.note: ADA Signal Processors; MIDI preamps and controllers.

PPG.note: Palm Products GmbH; OS EPROMs (Wave 2.2/2.3 OS V8.x; MIDI from the 2.3 and late 2.2 OS).

Fairlight.note: OS on floppy (QDOS/MDOS), ROMs on the CPU/MIDI cards.

Synclavier.note: New England Digital; system software on disk (Winchester/optical/floppy), MIDI from release N (1985).

Linn.note: Linn Electronics (1979-1986) and Roger Linn Design (2002-).

Simmons.note: Original Simmons (UK, 1978-1999); EPROM firmware and sound EPROMs.

Crumar.note: Bit synths made with Unique (Italy); modern Mojo/Seven have official updates.

GEM.note: Generalmusic; S-series/Equinox/Genesys load OS from disk or flash.

Ketron.note: Italian arrangers/modules; recent models have official OS downloads.

Viscount.note: Organs and modules; made Oberheim OB3/OB-12.

Hammond.note: Hammond-Suzuki digital organs; recent models (SK, XK-5) have official updates.

Technics.note: Matsushita/Panasonic keyboards (KN arrangers OS in mask ROM/flash).
Technics.status: partial: SX-PR pianos and home organs

Wersi.note: German organs (kits and finished); OAX organs update by official downloads.

Vermona.note: East German (VEB) instruments 1980s, HDB Vermona after 1990.

Jomox.note: Berlin; recent models have official firmware downloads.

Doepfer.note: Firmware mostly in PIC/EPROM; Doepfer publishes updates for some.

Kenton.note: UK; MIDI-CV converters, controllers and retrofit kits; firmware in PIC/EPROM, updates by chip or USB.

MOTU.note: Mark of the Unicorn; MTP/Express firmware in EPROM; USB models update with official ClockWorks/driver installers.

Opcode.note: Gibson bought Opcode in 1998; interfaces with EPROM firmware.

Midiman.note: Midiman became M-Audio in 2000 (later Avid, inMusic).

M-Audio.note: USB controllers; updates are official downloads.

Arturia.note: Firmware updates through MIDI Control Center / Arturia Software Center (official).

Teenage Engineering.note: Official firmware downloads for all MIDI products.

Studiologic.note: Fatar's brand; Sledge/Numa have official updates.

ARP.note: Pre-MIDI (company closed 1981); listed only because their firmware is in the collection.

Adafruit.note: Open-source TB-303 clone kit; firmware published on GitHub.

Creative.note: Sound cards with sound ROMs (E-mu EMU8000) and MIDI modules.

DKI.note: Digital Keyboards Inc. (Synergy, GDS); MIDI on later Synergy units.

Atari.note: Built-in MIDI ports; TOS in ROM.

Apple.note: Not a MIDI device; listed because its firmware is in the collection.

Tascam.note: Recorders/mixers with MIDI; later models have official updates.

Turtle Beach.note: Voyetra Turtle Beach; sound cards with sound ROMs or RAM-loaded firmware.

Allen Organ.note: Church organs with MIDI since the 1980s; only modules listed.

Encore Electronics.note: MIDI retrofit kits and MIDI-CV converters.

MIDI Solutions.note: Firmware updates are official SysEx downloads.

Native Instruments.note: USB controllers and Maschine+ standalone; official updates.

Synthstrom.note: Official firmware; open-source community firmware since 2024.

genoQs.note: Open-source firmware after the company closed.

Fender.note: Modelling amps with MIDI; Chroma Polaris is listed under Rhodes.

Dexibell.note: Italian (Proel group) digital pianos/organs; official updates.

Ahlborn.note: German church-organ maker; MIDI organ modules.

Lowrey.note: US home organs with MIDI (later Kawai-owned).

Kiwi Technics.note: Replacement CPU/MIDI kits for Roland/Korg classics; firmware updates by the maker.

Tubbutec.note: MIDI retrofit kits (firmware in the kit MCU).
